newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Tuesday:
Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the Commission would hold its weekly meeting on Wednesday at 1500/1400 GMT in Strasbourg.
Van der Pas said the Taxation Policy Group would hold its first meeting on Wednesday. He said Elisabetta Olivi would brief reporters at 1700/1600 GMT in her office.
Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan said the Commission had issued a memorandum explaining the acquired rights of workers in the case of transfer of undertakings.

Member of Commissioner Flynn's Cabinet Karen Banks said that in a German case of transfer of a cleaning lady, the Court had decided that a simple transfer of a contract would not be enough to make the directive 77/187/EEC on the maintenance of workers' rights applicable.
Nolan also said Commissioner Flynn wanted the Renault crisis to come to an end before proposing concrete new measures.

Asked about the flexibility of the criteria to enter the Economic and Monetary Union, in particular the one on public deficit, spokesman Patrick Child said when the time would come the Treaty would be strictly applied.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/199: Transfer of undertakings: Commission adopts a Memorandum explaining the acquired rights of workers.
- IP/97/200: Commissioner Bjerregaard welcomes consultative forum on the environment's recommendations on scenarios for a sustainable Europe in the year 2020.
- IP/97/201: First meeting of the taxation policy group.
- IP/97/202: Commissioner Franz Fischler today concludes six day visit in Japan.
- IP/97/203: Closure of Renault: statement by Commissioner Padraig Flynn to the European Parliament on Tuesday, 11 March 1997.
- IP/97/204: The Commission approves merger in business travel services.
- IP/97/206: Commissoner Edith Cresson to the European Parliament: human cloning should remain forbidden.
